AUTHOR'S OWN SERVING PATH on our rented hardware, run unmodified (revision a463f840c9259ff9139ab02181e01f20aca91b4b), inside the pinned vLLM image with the vLLM engine not used. NATIVE OUTPUTS: probabilities for choice, noul and score from marker-logit prefill; no generated text, reasoning, host retries or ensemble. CONFIGURATION: native batch size 8, max_batch_tokens 8192, permutation averaging 0 and temperature 1; no other setting was measured. TEXT ONLY: although the native health response advertises text and image, no image or video was passed and no multimodal result is claimed. CONTEXT AND REFUSALS: no configured input-length cap (max_length null), no truncation; the 8,192-token batching budget does not refuse a first long request. Public synthetic probes through 82,000 tokens passed before sealed input; this proves those probes, not unlimited context. ANSWERED: 1,500 of 1,500 (HTTP 200), 0 refusals, 0 native deviations; no stop. USAGE: input 964,081 tokens, equal to our first-party offline count exactly (0 usage mismatches), output 0 (zero-output convention). 10 s RULE: 5 decisions took over 10 s, the five long approximately 76,000-80,000-token items. All five were answered with HTTP 200 and remain answered in the native completion accounting under the frozen rules; the v1.7 share view applies its 10 s time-limit misses, whereas the frozen v1.6 and v1.7-off views apply no time limit. Measured loopback latency p50 0.086 s, p95 0.165 s, maximum 45.85 s over all 1,500 requests on one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 96 GB; scored loop about 356 s. Displayed self-hosted latency is an estimate under the shared method, not a measured hosted endpoint. Warm-up: public synthetic warm-up at every timed anchor and for long choice/score/255-option requests preceded timed smoke probes; a separate public pre-warm passed for the scored server before any sealed byte. DETERMINISM (record-only): the first 50 requests were run twice after scoring, 50 of 50 bit-identical, 0 argmax flips, maximum probability difference 0.0. HARDWARE: one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, nominal 96 GB; weights alone are 48.593 GiB. This is the measured device, not an empirically established minimum or a claim that a cheaper 80 GB card cannot fit. Licence: Apache-2.0 as declared on the model card; the repository has no root LICENSE file, and the included MIT licence covers only the inference code. TRAINING DATA: we did not inspect training data or verify overlap with JevBench public or sealed items, so contamination of the sealed draw is unchecked. Nothing in the reviewed author serving closure branches on benchmark item ids or gold answers (source review). ATTEMPT HISTORY: this is the one scored run for this row on this draw; all required pre-sealed gates passed before sealed input. Native deviations, usage comparison, replay and post-sealed health checks are record-only and do not retry or alter scored responses.
